title: Snapshot (full state roll-up)
description: DESCRIPTIVE, NOT NORMATIVE. Generated from firmware source at FW 1.8.0 and re-verified field by field against FW 2.1.4 (branch fix/2.1.4, release commit "chore(release): 2.1.4", whose parent is x-nearest-commit). x-source line numbers are from the 1.8.0 generation and are STALE; fields added or changed for 2.1.4 cite functions instead. This is not a specification and not a proposal; it records what the device emits today. Plane: D2C telemetry. `required` lists only keys present in the minimal payload, i.e. those always emitted for this message type.

schema.description: Wire-contract identifier. Constant; bump signals a breaking payload change. Range/enum: Fixed literal "eflostop.v2".

ts.description: Device wall-clock at message BUILD time. Built before the first clock sync (ts < 1704067200), this message is destroyed, never sent and never buffered; it is regenerated after connect. (Events are held and time-stamped instead, since 2.1.4.) Units: seconds (Unix epoch, UTC). Range/enum: >= 1704067200 (2024-01-01T00:00:00Z).

id.description: Immutable hub id derived from the WiFi STA MAC in eFuse. Same string used as the DPS registration id and the MQTT client id. Range/enum: "GW-" + 12 uppercase hex.

short_id.description: Last 2 bytes of the STA MAC as 4 hex chars. Also the SoftAP SSID suffix (WiFi-Hub-XXXX) the installer matches during setup. Range/enum: 4 uppercase hex chars.

name.description: User-assigned hub name from twin desired hub_name or C2D set_hub_name. NOTE the opposite convention on the twin plane, where hub_name is always emitted as "". Range/enum: free text, max 31 chars (HUB_NAME_MAX_LEN). Presence: conditional: OMITTED when the stored name is empty.

fw.description: Hub firmware version, read at runtime from the ESP-IDF app descriptor (PROJECT_VER). Never a hardcoded string. Range/enum: "2.1.4" for this release (CMakeLists.txt:12); "0.0.0" if the descriptor is empty.

uptime_s.description: Seconds since boot from the monotonic esp_timer. On an offline-buffer replay this is the ORIGINAL build-time value, possibly from a previous boot. Units: seconds. Range/enum: >= 0.

type.description: Envelope discriminator. Tells the backend which `data` shape to expect. Range/enum: enum: "lifecycle" | "snapshot" | "event".

reason.description: The trigger that caused this snapshot. Range/enum: heartbeat | event | commission | boot | fast | decommission. Since 2.1.4 a hub with NO devices publishes snapshots too: "event" for the transition to empty (e.g. the snapshot that follows the last decommission), "heartbeat" at the interval, and one "boot" per boot or MQTT (re)connect; the final snapshot before a decommission-all reboot keeps "decommission". Presence: always.
reason.x-source: snap_reason_str() and the single flush block in iothub_task(), main/iothub/app_iothub.c; "decommission" in the g_decommission_reboot block

rating.description: Worst rating across the provisioned devices. A leaking device is critical; a valve battery <= 10 % is critical (valve only; 11-20 % is warning); a latched leak interlock raises a warning floor while at least one device is provisioned. Devices never heard and still inside their own sync excuse are left out. "excellent" on a hub with no devices. Range/enum: excellent | good | warning | critical ("unknown" is not emitted in practice). Presence: always.

reason.description: Human-readable cause list for the rating. Free text for display, not parsing. Range/enum: max 191 chars. "No devices provisioned" on a hub with no devices (2.1.4). With rating excellent: "All devices healthy" or "Syncing - waiting for N device(s)". Otherwise a comma-joined list, most urgent first, drawn from: "Leak detected: <label>" | "N leaks detected" | "Leak interlock latched" | one of "Valve offline" / "Valve disconnected" / "Valve battery critical" (2.1.4) / "Valve battery low" | "N sensor(s) offline" | "N sensor(s) battery low" | "N sensor(s) signal weak" | "syncing N device(s)"; "Degraded" as the fallback. The rating and the reason are sampled under one lock, so they cannot disagree. ("Health data unavailable" is gone: since 2.1.4 a snapshot is not published at all when the health table is busy.) Presence: always.

system_health.description: Fleet roll-up container: the single worst device rating plus a human-readable cause. Presence: always (snapshot only).

valve_id.description: The PROVISIONED valve's MAC (from the health table, which is reconciled against provisioning). Never the live link's MAC. Range/enum: uppercase colon-separated MAC. Presence: whenever a valve is provisioned; the whole object is {} when none is (2.1.4).

state.description: Valve position, or the link state. open | closed from a live, GATT-ready link to the provisioned valve; "unknown" while that link is up but not yet GATT-ready (2.1.4), or when the characteristic byte is neither 0 nor 1; "disconnected" when there is no live link to the provisioned valve. Presence: whenever valve_id is present.

battery.description: Valve battery. null until the valve is GATT-ready, and when no real reading exists on this link (0xFF); never 0 for unknown (2.1.4, BUG-1). Units: percent. Range/enum: 0..100 when a number. Presence: when connected is true; ABSENT when connected is false.
battery.x-source: valve block of telemetry_v2_publish_snapshot() main/telemetry/telemetry_v2.c; g_val_battery 0xFF main/ble_valve/app_ble_valve.c

leak_state.description: Water detected AT THE VALVE body (its own flood probe), distinct from the remote leak sensors. Reads the module's cached value, which is false until the first read on this link. Presence: when connected is true; ABSENT when connected is false.

rmleak.description: The valve's remote-leak interlock latch. While true the valve refuses to open, and the hub refuses a valve_open command. Presence: when connected is true; ABSENT when connected is false.
rmleak.x-source: ble_valve_get_rmleak_state() in telemetry_v2_publish_snapshot(); open refusal valve_open_reject_reason() main/iothub/app_iothub.c

connected.description: true only for a live link to the PROVISIONED valve (MAC match). A link that is up but not yet GATT-ready also reads true, with state "unknown" and battery null. Presence: whenever valve_id is present.

fw_version.description: Valve firmware revision from the BLE Device Information Service, copied verbatim. Range/enum: free text, max 31 chars. Presence: string when read; explicit null when connected but not read; ABSENT when connected is false.

rating.description: Valve health rating: link (WARNING grace, then CRITICAL), battery (<= 10 % critical, 11-20 % warning, 2.1.4) and the valve's own flood probe (wet = critical). Presence: whenever valve_id is present.

last_seen_age_s.description: The valve's link age. Since 2.1.4 it is 0 while the BLE link to the provisioned valve is up (link supervision drops a link that stops answering, so a linked valve is being heard now), and once disconnected the seconds since the link dropped. Up to 2.1.3 it was the seconds since the valve's last changed value or connect, which grew for hours on a steady, connected valve. Units: seconds. Range/enum: >= 0 when a number. Presence: whenever valve_id is present; explicit null when never seen this uptime.

valve.description: The PROVISIONED valve. {} (empty object) when no valve is provisioned (2.1.4, BUG-5); before 2.1.4 a valve-less hub sent {"state":"disconnected","connected":false} and a valve still linked during its removal was published live (BUG-3). Live data (battery, leak_state, rmleak, fw_version) only from a link to the provisioned MAC. Presence: always (snapshot only).

sensor_id.description: LoRa sensor id as rendered by the health engine. Range/enum: "0x" + 8 uppercase hex, e.g. 0x754A6237. Presence: always for each element.

connected.description: Heard within the health timeout. Also gates the telemetry-cache merge (snr). Presence: always.

rating.description: Health rating from timeout + battery + RSSI thresholds. Range/enum: enum: excellent | good | warning | critical | unknown. Presence: always for each element.

last_seen_age_s.description: Seconds since this sensor last checked in. Units: seconds. Range/enum: >= 0 when a number. Presence: always present; explicit null when UINT32_MAX (never heard).

battery.description: Battery from the HEALTH table, updated on every check-in. Units: percent. Range/enum: 0..100 when a number. Presence: always present; explicit null until the device's first reading since it was added (0xFF).

leak_state.description: The health engine's wet/dry for this sensor, connected or not: an offline sensor that was last wet stays true, matching system_health.reason. Range/enum: true | false. Presence: always present.

rssi.description: RSSI of the last check-in, from the HEALTH table. Units: dBm. Presence: always present; explicit null until the first check-in since the device was added (0). LoRa values can wrap positive (int8_t narrowing in the SX127x driver).

snr.description: LoRa SNR of the last cached D2C event, merged only while connected. Quarter-dB steps (the only non-integer number on the wire). Units: dB. Presence: always present; null when not connected or no cache entry.

code.description: Machine-readable room code from the sensor_meta table; "unknown" when no metadata is stored. Range/enum: enum, 13 values.

label.description: User-entered free-text location label. Range/enum: free text, max 31 chars; "" when no metadata is stored.

location.description: Installed-location metadata. Presence: always for each element (never omitted).

lora_sensors.description: One entry per PROVISIONED LoRa leak sensor, driven by the health table (not the radio cache). Every key is always present; unknown values are null. Presence: always; [] when none (2.1.4: an empty hub publishes [] for both arrays).

sensor_id.description: BLE leak sensor MAC as rendered by the health engine. Range/enum: colon-separated MAC. Presence: always for each element.

connected.description: Heard within the health timeout. Also gates the telemetry-cache merge (fw_version). Presence: always.

rating.description: Health rating from timeout + battery + RSSI thresholds. Range/enum: enum: excellent | good | warning | critical | unknown. Presence: always for each element.

last_seen_age_s.description: Seconds since this sensor's last advertisement was accepted. Units: seconds. Range/enum: >= 0 when a number. Presence: always present; explicit null when UINT32_MAX (never heard).

battery.description: Battery from the HEALTH table, updated on every check-in. Units: percent. Range/enum: 0..100 when a number. Presence: always present; explicit null until the device's first reading since it was added (0xFF).

leak_state.description: The health engine's wet/dry for this sensor, connected or not: an offline sensor that was last wet stays true, matching system_health.reason. Range/enum: true | false. Presence: always present.

rssi.description: RSSI of the last check-in, from the HEALTH table. Units: dBm. Presence: always present; explicit null until the first check-in since the device was added (0).

fw_version.description: Sensor firmware version from the telemetry cache, merged only while connected. Range/enum: "M.m.p". Presence: always present; null when not connected, no cache entry, or the advertisement carries no version.

code.description: Machine-readable room code from the sensor_meta table; "unknown" when no metadata is stored. Range/enum: enum, 13 values.

label.description: User-entered free-text location label. Range/enum: free text, max 31 chars; "" when no metadata is stored.

location.description: Installed-location metadata. Presence: always for each element (never omitted).

ble_leak_sensors.description: One entry per PROVISIONED BLE leak sensor, driven by the health table (not the radio cache). Every key is always present; unknown values are null. Presence: always; [] when none (2.1.4: an empty hub publishes [] for both arrays).

auto_close_enabled.description: Master switch: does a leak automatically close the valve. Range/enum: true | false. Presence: present whenever data.rules is present.

trigger_mask.description: Which leak sources may trigger auto-close. bit0=BLE leak, bit1=LoRa, bit2=valve flood. NOTHING masks or validates the inbound value, so the emitted range is 0..255, not 0..7. Units: bitmask. Range/enum: 0..255 on the wire (only bits 0-2 are interpreted). Presence: present whenever data.rules is present.
trigger_mask.x-source: main/telemetry/telemetry_v2.c:362, :581; bits main/provisioning_manager/provisioning_manager.h:22-25; unmasked cast main/rules_engine/rules_engine.c:562 and main/provisioning_manager/provisioning_manager.c:486

rules.description: Global auto-close configuration container. Byte-identical shape in lifecycle and snapshot so the backend reuses one parser. Presence: conditional: OMITTED if provisioning_get_rules_config() fails (mutex timeout / not initialised).

override_active.description: Is the 24 h water-access override window open (auto-close suppressed). Range/enum: true | false. Presence: always (snapshot only).

override_remaining_s.description: Seconds left in the override window, and 0 when expired but not yet processed by the rules tick. A window started before the clock synced is measured on the hub uptime until the rules tick re-bases it to the synced clock, within about 30 s of the sync (2.1.4); a window restored from an earlier unsynced power cycle reads 0 until that tick ends it. A window with a real expiry restored after a power-on that lost the clock counts down from that power-on until the clock syncs (2.1.4; it used to read the full duration), and expires_ts is omitted meanwhile. Units: seconds. Range/enum: >= 0 when present. Presence: snapshot: OMITTED unless override_active AND remaining >= 0. auto_close_blocked_override event: OMITTED when remaining < 0.

expires_ts.description: Absolute epoch at which the override window expires. Same field name and meaning on both message types. Units: seconds (Unix epoch, UTC). Range/enum: >= 1704067200. Presence: snapshot: OMITTED unless override_active AND the expiry is known and in the future, so also OMITTED for a window started before the clock synced until the rules tick re-bases it (2.1.4). water_access_override_enabled event: OMITTED when the window was started before the clock synced (2.1.4), present otherwise.

data.description: Type-specific payload container. Since 2.1.4 every container is attached on creation and NULL-checked: on an allocation failure, or when the health table is busy, the snapshot is not published at all (no partial snapshot). Presence: always.
